nodes.summary: There is a natural number $N$ such that no finite set of residue classes covering $\mathbb{Z}$ has pairwise distinct moduli that are all at least $N$. Hence the conjecture of Open Garden problem OPG-493 is false.
nodes.title: Hough's minimum modulus theorem

nodes.summary: The statement that for every natural number $N$ there are finitely many residue classes $a_1 \bmod m_1, \dots, a_k \bmod m_k$ that cover $\mathbb{Z}$ (every integer lies in at least one of them) whose moduli are pairwise distinct and all at least $N$.
nodes.title: Covering systems with arbitrarily large distinct moduli (OPG-493)
Replacing the largest prime factor of the modulus set

nodes.summary: There is a distinct covering system, that is, a finite set of congruences $x \equiv r \pmod m$ with $r \in \mathbb{Z}$, $m \in \mathbb{N}$ and no two with the same modulus, such that every integer satisfies at least one of them, whose moduli are all at least $7$, include $7$, and have least common multiple $15120$.
nodes.title: A distinct covering system with minimum modulus 7 and moduli of lcm 15120

nodes.summary: There is a distinct covering system, that is, a finite set of congruences $x \equiv r \pmod m$ with $r \in \mathbb{Z}$, $m \in \mathbb{N}$ and no two with the same modulus, such that every integer satisfies at least one of them, whose moduli all lie between $6$ and $168$ and include both $6$ and $168$.
nodes.title: A distinct covering system with moduli from 6 to 168

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be a covering system with positive moduli: a finite set of congruences $x \equiv r \pmod m$ with $r \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $m \ge 1$ such that every integer satisfies at least one of them. Let $p$ be a prime and $a \ge 1$, and suppose exactly $p$ congruences of $C$ have modulus divisible by $p^a$, with moduli $p^a m_1, \dots, p^a m_p$. nodes.title: Merging the p classes whose modulus is divisible by a prime power

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be a distinct covering system: a finite set of congruences $x \equiv r \pmod m$ with $r \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $m \in \mathbb{N}$, no two with the same modulus, such that every integer satisfies at least one of them. If every modulus of $C$ is at least $5$ and some modulus equals $5$, then some modulus of $C$ is at least $108$.
nodes.title: Krukenberg's conjecture for minimum modulus five

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be a distinct covering system: a finite set of congruences $x \equiv r \pmod m$ with $r \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $m \in \mathbb{N}$ (where $x \equiv r \pmod 0$ means $x = r$), no two with the same modulus, such that every integer satisfies at least one of them. Let $B \in \mathbb{N}$ be at least every modulus of $C$, let $p$ be a prime and $a \ge 1$. If $B < p^a (p + 1)$, then the congruences of $C$ whose…
nodes.title: Discarding the classes whose modulus is divisible by a large prime power

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be a covering system with positive moduli: a finite set of congruences $x \equiv a \pmod m$ with $a \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $m \ge 1$ such that every integer satisfies at least one of them. Let $L$ be the least common multiple of its moduli, $p$ a prime dividing $L$, and $a_1 < a_2 \le p - 1$ natural numbers. nodes.title: Swapping two residues modulo a prime in a covering system

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be a covering system: a finite set of congruences $x \equiv a_i \pmod{m_i}$ with $a_i \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $m_i \in \mathbb{N}$ (where $x \equiv a_i \pmod 0$ means $x = a_i$) such that every integer satisfies at least one of them. Then for every $t \in \mathbb{Z}$ the congruences $x \equiv a_i + t \pmod{m_i}$ also form a covering system.
nodes.title: Translating a covering system

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be a distinct covering system: a finite set of congruences $x \equiv r \pmod m$ with $r \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $m \in \mathbb{N}$, no two with the same modulus, such that every integer satisfies at least one of them. If every modulus of $C$ is at least $5$ and some modulus equals $5$, then the least common multiple of the moduli of $C$ is at least $1440$.
nodes.title: Least common multiple of a covering system with minimum modulus five

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be a distinct covering system: a finite set of congruences $x \equiv r \pmod m$ with $r \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $m \in \mathbb{N}$, no two with the same modulus, such that every integer satisfies at least one of them. If every modulus of $C$ is at least $6$ and some modulus equals $6$, then the least common multiple of the moduli of $C$ is at least $5040$.
nodes.title: Least common multiple of a covering system with minimum modulus six

nodes.summary: Let $a_1 \bmod m_1, \dots, a_k \bmod m_k$ be residue classes that cover $\mathbb{Z}$, that is, every integer lies in at least one of them. If the moduli $m_1, \dots, m_k$ are pairwise distinct and all at least $2$, then $\sum_{i=1}^{k} 1/m_i > 1$.
nodes.title: Mirsky–Newman bound for distinct covering systems

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
